tasks.title: Create ngv2/selection_ranker.py: hard 5-gate filter merged with saturation-dominant soft score
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/selection_ranker.py exists and contains EXACTLY the content given in the brief Deliverables (verbatim, byte-for-byte).
Module imports `qualify as _qualify` from ngv2.target_qualify and invokes it per candidate rather than reimplementing the 5-gate.
`rank_candidates` drops every non-GO candidate (SKIP/UNKNOWN) and returns only GO survivors.

`score_candidate` produces saturation-dominant scores: 0 subs -> +25, <=3 -> +20, <=10 -> +12, <=20 -> +5, else 0; bounty minor (>=1500 -> +10, >=900 -> +7, >=600 -> +5, >0 -> +3, else +1); freshness by audit age; capped at 100.
Same-CWE dedup zeroes the marginal bounty contribution when the candidate's CWE is already in `known_cwes`.
Returned queue is a list of (repo, score, oracle_result) sorted by score descending then repo name.
Module is pure: stdlib + ngv2 only; no network, clock, disk, subprocess, randomness, or threading; no other module is touched.
Verification command passes: the committed oracle tests/test_selection_ranker_wired.py is green.

spec.objective: Add a NEW pure, stdlib+ngv2-only module ngv2/selection_ranker.py that turns a list of injected bounty candidates into a deterministic ranked work queue by merging the live HARD 5-gate (ngv2.target_qualify.qualify) with the saturation-dominant SOFT priority score ported from legacy services/tools/target_priority_scorer.py. Emit the file exactly as specified in the brief Deliverables.
functional_requirements: Create ngv2/selection_ranker.py whose content matches the brief Deliverables verbatim (module docstring, imports, four private weight functions, score_candidate, rank_candidates).

Import qualify from ngv2.target_qualify aliased as _qualify and call _qualify(repo, cwe, severity, purpose, bounty=..., submissions=..., days_ago=..., fp_patterns=...) per candidate; do NOT reimplement the gate.
_bounty_score(expected_payout) returns the deliberately MINOR table: >=1500 -> 10, >=900 -> 7, >=600 -> 5, >0 -> 3, else 1.
score_candidate sums saturation + (0 if cwe_already_seen else bounty) + freshness, capped to a maximum of 100.

rank_candidates resolves per-candidate cwe/severity overrides (defaulting to args), extracts expected_payout robustly from the injected bounty mapping (None/non-int -> 0), derives cwe_seen by case-insensitive match against known_cwes, drops non-GO results, and appends (repo, score, oracle_result).
rank_candidates returns the GO-only queue sorted by score descending then repo name ascending; the full target_qualify result dict is carried as oracle_result.
spec.interfaces: Exposes `rank_candidates(candidates, *, cwe='CWE-94', severity='HIGH', purpose='hunt') -> list[(repo, score, oracle_result)]` (GO survivors only, sorted score desc then repo) and `score_candidate(expected_payout, submissions, days_since_audit, *, cwe_already_seen=False) -> int` (saturation-dominant 0..100). Private helpers: _saturation_score, _bounty_score, _freshness_score.
edge_cases: bounty is None or not a Mapping -> expected_payout treated as 0 (bounty score becomes +1).
expected_payout is a non-numeric/non-int value -> coerced to 0 without raising.
submissions missing or falsy -> treated as 0 (virgin target, +25).
days_ago is None -> freshness +5; days_ago < 7 already excluded by the gate but freshness table still returns 0.
known_cwes absent/empty -> no dedup; CWE comparison is case-insensitive and whitespace-stripped.
Ties in score resolved deterministically by ascending repo name.
Score that would exceed 100 (e.g. 25+10+10=45 cannot, but guard still applies) is clamped to 100.
Mixed GO / SKIP / UNKNOWN inputs -> only GO rows appear in the output.
non_goals: Do NOT reimplement or modify target_qualify, bounty_gate, batch_qualify, or source_qualify_gate.
No scraping, file reads, network, or clock access; every fact is an injected candidate field.
No LLM, subprocess, randomness, or threading.
Touch no module other than the single new file ngv2/selection_ranker.py.
spec.implementation_notes:
Emit the file exactly as in the brief Deliverables — content is fully specified and must not drift. Keep `from __future__ import annotations` and the typing imports. The legacy weight tables encode the 'pickle fatigue' lesson: saturation dominates bounty, and same-CWE prior work zeroes the marginal bounty credit so already-mined targets sink in the ranking.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Synthetic candidate mappings with injected bounty decision dicts (decision/expected_payout), submissions counts spanning the saturation buckets, days_ago spanning freshness buckets, fp_patterns lists, optional cwe/severity overrides, and known_cwes sets to exercise dedup. Mixed GO/SKIP/UNKNOWN candidates to verify filtering and ordering.

token_budget_ratio.note: Implementation is a verbatim file emission; the bulk of effort is the oracle test that pins gate-wiring, weight tables, dedup, and ordering.

tasks.title: Author oracle tests/test_selection_ranker_wired.py for ngv2.selection_ranker
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_selection_ranker_wired.py exists and is the committed oracle named in the verification command.
Tests call the live ngv2.target_qualify.qualify through rank_candidates (no mocking of the gate) to prove the 5-gate wiring.
Tests assert non-GO candidates (SKIP/UNKNOWN) are dropped from the queue.
Tests pin every saturation, bounty, and freshness weight boundary and the 100 cap.
Tests prove same-CWE dedup zeroes the marginal bounty contribution.
Tests prove the queue is sorted by score descending then repo name ascending and carries the full oracle_result dict.
Full suite passes: cd /home/xnihil0zer0/NobleGreedv2 && .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_selection_ranker_wired.py -q.

spec.objective: Author the committed oracle test module tests/test_selection_ranker_wired.py that exercises ngv2.selection_ranker end to end against the live ngv2.target_qualify.qualify, pinning the hard-gate filtering, the saturation-dominant soft weights, the same-CWE dedup/consolidation, and deterministic ordering.
functional_requirements: Verify rank_candidates filters out every non-GO (SKIP/UNKNOWN) candidate while keeping GO survivors, using the real qualify gate (no gate mocking).
Verify the saturation table boundaries via score_candidate / rank output: 0->+25, 3->+20, 10->+12, 20->+5, 21->+0.
Verify the minor bounty table boundaries: 1500->+10, 900->+7, 600->+5, 1->+3, 0->+1.
Verify the freshness table: None->+5, <7->0, <30->+3, <90->+5, <365->+8, >=365->+10, and that score is capped at 100.
Verify same-CWE dedup zeroes the bounty contribution when the candidate CWE is present in known_cwes (case-insensitive), and does not when absent.

Verify the output is a list of (repo, score, oracle_result) sorted by score descending then repo name ascending, with oracle_result being the full target_qualify result dict, and that a virgin 0-submission target outranks a high-bounty saturated one.
spec.interfaces: Imports ngv2.selection_ranker.rank_candidates and ngv2.selection_ranker.score_candidate; constructs injected candidate mappings (repo, bounty decision dict, submissions, days_ago, fp_patterns, optional cwe/severity/known_cwes); asserts against returned (repo, score, oracle_result) tuples.
edge_cases: Candidate with bounty=None still scores (+1 bounty) when GO.
Candidate with non-int expected_payout coerces to 0 without raising.
known_cwes given with differing case/whitespace still triggers dedup.
Two GO candidates with identical scores tie-break by ascending repo name.
A SKIP-on-saturation candidate is absent from the queue even with otherwise high soft inputs.
non_goals: Do not mock or patch ngv2.target_qualify.qualify; exercise the live gate.
Do not modify ngv2/selection_ranker.py or any other module from the test.
No network, subprocess, randomness, or threading in the test.
spec.implementation_notes: The mutation gate will mutate ngv2.selection_ranker (e.g. flip a weight boundary, drop the dedup zeroing, or remove the non-GO filter); the authored tests MUST fail against such a mutant. Cover each weight boundary and the dedup/order invariants with tight assertions so the suite is non-vacuous.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Hand-built candidate mappings covering each saturation/bounty/freshness boundary, GO/SKIP/UNKNOWN gate outcomes, known_cwes sets for dedup (including mixed case), and tie-break repo names. No fixtures requiring IO; all facts injected inline.

token_budget_ratio.note: This task is the oracle itself; nearly all effort is authoring the wired test assertions that kill the declared mutant.
